headline: Trump names his sixth press secretary
summary: Katie Zacharia, 42, a lawyer and TV commentator, is Trump's pick for White House press secretary, the sixth across his two terms. Since June she has advised Trump's media company, which runs Truth Social. She spent two months this year as a Homeland Security spokesperson. Karoline Leavitt left the job in August.
cover_answer: She takes the reporters' questions so he doesn't have to.
table_question: Who should speak for you when you can't be there?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president picked a new helper whose job is to answer reporters' questions every day. Her name is Katie Zacharia, and she has four kids. It's like being the kid at the front of the class who explains what the teacher decided. Nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: A helper with a job and four kids. The podium can wait.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reads a parent's face before the words, so the script gives one helper, one job, and four kids of her own, the detail this age will keep. The front-of-class picture is a mechanism they know. Expect "why can't the president just talk?" He does. Reporters ask all day, and that is her job now.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Karoline Leavitt left the White House podium in August. Trump picked Katie Zacharia, a lawyer at his media company, as his sixth press secretary in two terms. The team captain who talks to the referee: the players decide, the captain explains.
8-12.why: Someone left, someone was picked, sixth in the job.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script runs one chain: Leavitt left in August, Trump picked Zacharia, she is the sixth. The captain who talks to the referee is one every kid who plays has seen. Expect "why so many?" People leave, and the president picks the next one. The articles don't say why.

13-17.script: Should the president's spokesperson come from his own company? Katie Zacharia advises Trump Media, and now she'll take the White House podium. Second: she told the BBC a good UFC fight sums up the American ethos. What does the messenger tell you about the message?
13-17.why: Does the messenger match the message? Let them run it.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can reason about what is not in front of them: a spokesperson paid by the president's company, then by the public, and whether that is one job or two. The script hands over her own words on UFC and lets them judge the choice. Expect "aren't they all loyal?" Yes. The question is who signs the cheque.

5-7.a: Someone whose job is to ask questions and tell everyone the answers. There are lots of them at the White House every day.

8-12.a: He does some. Reporters ask all day, and she answers for the White House.
Six across his two presidencies. The last, Karoline Leavitt, left in August.

13-17.q: Isn't it odd she works for his company?
13-17.a: Trump Media runs Truth Social and pays her. Next, the public pays her.
No. A lawyer and a TV commentator, on the president's side of the room.
